## SECURITIES AND FUTURES COMMISSION

12th Floor, Edinburgh Tower, The Landmark, 15 Queen's Road Central, Hong Kong

16 August 2001

## Circular to Brokers

## Suspected Fraud by Walk-In Clients

The  Commission  has  recently  received  several  reports  from  intermediaries  on suspected fraudulent activities that may expose them to financial losses. The modus operandi of the suspected fraudulent activities is as follows:

- walk-in  clients  opened  securities  accounts  with  the  intermediaries  and  shortly after the accounts were opened, placed orders to buy shares in a listed security;
- when required by the intermediaries to  deposit  the  funds  for  the  purchases,  the walk-in  clients  would  produce  pay-in  slips  which  showed  funds  had  been deposited into the intermediaries' bank accounts by cheques;
- after  the  purchases  were  concluded,  the  intermediaries  were    advised  by  their bankers (usually immediately after the market close) that the cheques deposited by the walk-in clients had bounced at which time it was found that these cheques were issued by third parties;
- the  walk-in  clients,  however,  could  not  be  located  as  the    personal  information provided by them to the intermediaries was fake.

The Commission would like to draw the attention of intermediaries to these fraudulent activities.  It  is  in  the  interest  of  intermediaries  to  ensure  they  observe  the  rule regarding  'Know  Your  Clients'  and  put  in  place  satisfactory  internal  control procedures to protect their operations from financial loss arising from fraud and other dishonest acts.  Particularly when dealing with new clients, brokers should exercise caution and ensure they have cleared funds to satisfy orders.

Intermediaries &amp; Investment Products Securities &amp; Futures Commission
